observation_summary: The methods getDomainAxisIndex and getRangeAxisIndex in CategoryPlot were failing to handle null arguments, causing unexpected behavior when null was passed, as evidenced by the failing tests which expected an IllegalArgumentException.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding an explicit null check at the beginning of the methods to validate the input parameter 'axis'. This is a classic example of a missing guard/validation check, which falls under the 'Checking' category in ODC.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of 'if (axis == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException(...); }' in both getDomainAxisIndex and getRangeAxisIndex.
The test code snippets show that the tests were specifically designed to expect an IllegalArgumentException when passing null to these methods (e.g., lines 755-761 in CategoryPlotTests.java).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix is not changing the computational logic of the index lookup, but rather adding a guard to validate the input before the lookup occurs.
